newsitem.title: UK: Death toll in Russian blast rises to 42 - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Death toll in Russian blast rises to 42 - Tass.

text.p: The death toll from the weekend explosion at a military block of flats in Russia's southern Dagestan region rose to 42 on Monday, Itar-Tass news agency reported.

Tass, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, quoted a spokesman for the Ministry for Emergency Situations as saying the dead from Saturday's blast included 15 children. The death toll stood at 24 on Sunday evening.
The agency said rescue operations to find another 14 people believed to be still trapped in the rubble were continuing.
Rescue workers have been frantically sifting through the ruins of the block for survivors of the explosion, which border guards said was an attempt by gangsters to scare the authorities.
A spokesman for Dagestani authorities said on Sunday eight injured people had been pulled from the ruins of the eight- storey building.
Tass quoted official sources as saying it might be a gangland revenge attack linked to a regional crackdown on arms and caviar smuggling.
The border guards issued a statement describing the explosion as a "terrorist act" by cross-border criminals.
"Those who thus intend to intimidate the border defenders are deeply mistaken," it said, adding that the losses had strengthened their resolve to deal harshly with the criminals.
It called on the relevant state institutions to deal with the "outrageous outburst of crime and terrorism" in the country.

Gangland violence has become commonplace in post-communist Russia. Earlier this month 14 people died in a bomb blast at a Moscow cemetery apparently triggered by a feud between warring factions of an Afghan war veterans' charity with big business links.
Regional authorities declared Sunday and Monday official days of mourning in Dagestan, which borders the breakaway Russian republic of Chechnya.
Some officials said there might be a link between the explosion and Chechnya, where an uneasy peace is holding after a 21-month bloody conflict between Russian forces and separatists.

But Chechen rebel leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev, whose aide worked out a new draft agreement with Moscow on Saturday, denied the separatists were involved in the blast, which he said was aimed at wrecking the peace process.

The border guards said the blast could not have been caused by a gas leak because the building was not connected to gas mains. Agencies reported signs that TNT explosive had been detonated in the building.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from heart surgery, has sent his condolences to relatives of the dead and the government has set up a commission under a deputy prime minister, Oleg Lobov, to investigate the causes of the blast.
